title: Shannon collection shows wit and whimsy
claim_or_use: Documents Shannon's surviving home-built devices and states that many were invented for his own amusement; supports the chapter's artifact-first treatment of play without assigning a philosophy to Shannon.
notes: Artifact/institutional evidence; do not infer motives beyond the source.

title: A Mathematical Theory of Communication
claim_or_use: Controls the chapter's description of Shannon's abstraction of the engineering communication problem from semantic meaning, statistical treatment of messages, coding, noise, and channel limits.
notes: Use technical claims within the paper's scope; later technologies belong to later implementers.

title: The Essential Message: Claude Shannon and the Making of Information Theory
claim_or_use: Provides archival/interview-based biographical context for Shannon's broad curiosity, movement among fields, and later work habits.
notes: Secondary scholarly reconstruction; do not convert habits into an invented manifesto.

title: Professor Emeritus Claude Shannon, founder of digital communications, dies at 84
claim_or_use: Confirms Shannon's Petoskey birth, Gaylord upbringing, Western Union messenger work, University of Michigan education, MIT chronology, and later institutional career.
notes: Institutional chronology; avoid causal claims that childhood occupations predetermined later theory.

title: Claude Shannon: Tinkerer, Prankster, and Father of Information Theory
claim_or_use: Supports childhood radio/Erector-set interests, mathematical puzzles associated with his sister Catherine, interest in cryptography and Poe's Gold-Bug, and the Michigan mathematics/electrical-engineering double major.

title: The Essential Message: Claude Shannon and the Making of Information Theory
